**Triage** — graded `p3`, `finding` cleared, `pm:queue`, routed `domain:services`. No type label: it is neither a bug nor docs, and ⛔ this seat does not mint new labels.

## Your claim is exact, and I can tighten it to a closed count

At `origin/main` `2aa8456`:

- `policy.redactFields` has **exactly one reader in the whole file** — `share-link-service.ts:772`, the union `[...(policy.redactFields ?? []), ...(row.redact_fields ?? [])]`.
- The `[#14033]` gate `if (!policy.enabled)` is at `:697`, **75 lines above it**, and returns.
- `getPolicy` has **exactly two callers**: `:442` (`createLink`) and `:650` (`resolveToken`). `createLink` reads `enabled` (`:449`), `allowedPermissions` (`:458`), `allowedAudiences` (`:467`) and `eligibility` (`:498`) — and at `:545` writes `input.redactFields`, the caller's, never `policy.redactFields`.

So: one reader, unreachable when the switch is off, and no second consumer anywhere. The disabled branch's read is dead exactly as you say, and the `[#13856]` comment at `:103-104` describes a case that no longer exists.

## Disposition: take option 2 — keep the read, fix the comment

You said either is fine and no behaviour depends on it, which is true. I am ruling it anyway rather than leaving it to the implementer, because the two options age differently.

**Option 1 (collapse to `redactFields: []`) makes the safety of the redaction set depend on a single gate.** Today that gate is sound. But the read is free, it fails **closed**, and #13856 exists precisely because the empty version once let an opt-out widen what a live token served. Deleting a cheap fail-closed read to tidy a branch is the trade that looks clean in the diff and bad in the incident.

⭐ The sharper reason is on the neighbouring card: **#14637** measures that the route layer already re-opens an existence oracle this same service deliberately closed — i.e. a property held by one gate in this file is, in practice, defeated one layer up. That is a live demonstration that "the gate above it returns first" is a weaker guarantee here than it reads. Keep the belt.

So: **leave the read, rewrite the comment.** It should stop describing "tokens that still serve on a switched-off block" (no such token exists after #14033) and start saying what is true — that the branch is defence in depth behind the `:697` redemption gate, kept so a future change to that gate cannot silently strip an object's declared redactions. Cite #14033 alongside #13856; the history is the point of the comment.

## Scope

⛔ Comment only. No behaviour change, no test change — you note the four #14171 pins that read the set with the switch off are already reversed and registered, and the `enabled: true` control pin stays. Nothing in this card touches them.

⛔ Do not fold in #14637. Same file, different function, and that one is `needs-user-decision` pending a maintainer ruling — it cannot be dispatched yet, so there is no collision today. If it is ruled and dispatched before this lands, the two seats should compare file surfaces first: `getPolicy`/`resolveToken`'s policy branch here, `share-link-routes.ts` + the runtime twin there.

⛔ Do not re-open #14171's `redactFields` logic. #14033's dispatch fenced it (「`redactFields` 半边在 #13856 已派发,⛔ 不合卡、不重做」) and this card inherits that fence.

## On the filing

Recording it instead of folding it into the #14033 PR was right, and for the reason you give: the ruling said the sibling keys are **moot**, not that their reads must be removed. Reading a "moot" ruling as licence to delete is how a PR ends up wider than the ruling that authorised it.

## Claim: `domain:services` execution seat

- **Session** — `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8` (`os-sales`) · **Branch** `claude/issue-14581-getpolicy-disabled-redactfields` · **Worktree** `objectstack-issue-14581`, cut `--no-track` from `origin/main` `7a17f3bf1` · **Round** R16
- **File surface** — `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts` and `share-link-service.test.ts`.
- **Serial constraints** — `plugin-sharing` has two open PRs of this seat and **neither holds these files**: PR #14528 holds `rule-hooks.ts` / `sharing-plugin.ts` / `bu-tree-recompute.ts`; PR #14726 holds `sharing-service.ts` and the backfill module. ⛔ Out of fence for this card, all five. ⚠️ Both of those PRs do move `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` — the repo's two hottest generated files — so if this diff moves either, merge `origin/main` first, **commit the merge**, then re-derive with the generator. ⛔ Never hand-edit an anchor or a ledger row.
- **Container & model** — opus. Derived on `origin/main`: `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier` reports no path-derived mandate for `plugin-sharing/src`; judged opus because the question here is which of two dispositions is right, not how to type it.
- **Clause ②** — expected **`no`** (a read removed inside a module-private helper), and the dev re-derives it from the actual diff with `git diff -U0 origin/main...HEAD | grep -E '^\+\s*export '` plus a signature check on anything already exported. Over-conservative `yes` costs a label; a wrong `no` defeats a gate.
- **Ruling of record** — the #14033 ruling of 2026-09-01, quoted verbatim and untranslated, is what made this read dead:

  > 「`enabled` 关 ⇒ 整块不生效 ⇒ 拒付(子键求值 moot)」

  ⚠️ It says the sibling keys are **moot**, not that their reads must be deleted. Removing the read is therefore housekeeping the ruling permits, **not** something it commands — so it must not change behaviour, and if it would, stop.

### Disposition — take route 1, and prove it is inert

The card offers two. Take **route 1**: collapse the disabled branch to `redactFields: []` and rewrite the comment to cite #14033 (the redemption gate is what now keeps opt-out from widening anything). Route 2 (delete only the stale comment) leaves a read whose only justification is a case that cannot occur — that is how dead code with a confident comment survives another year.

**Premise-first stop conditions.** Any one firing ⇒ commit, push, report on this card, stop:

1. **The read is not dead.** The card's claim is that after #14033's gate, `resolveToken()` returns before the `policy.redactFields` union and `createLink()` never reads it. Verify **both** on `origin/main` — the #14033 PR has since landed, so this is now checkable on the merged tree rather than on a branch. If any live caller reaches that branch, the card is wrong and the read stays.
2. **Removing it moves a test.** The four #14171 pins that read the set with the switch OFF are described as already reversed and registered. If collapsing the branch reds anything beyond those, you have found behaviour, not dead code.
3. **`getPolicy` is exported.** Then this is a public-surface question, not housekeeping — stop and say so; Clause ② would flip.

### What "done" means

- The `enabled !== true` branch no longer reads `raw.redactFields`, and the comment beside it describes **#14033's redemption gate** rather than the #13856 case that can no longer arise.
- The `enabled: true` control pin still passes untouched — that is the pin proving you removed only the dead half.
- Exact `Tests N failed | M passed (T)` for `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing test`, before and after.
- Changeset: judge it. A dead-read removal with no behaviour change normally owes none; `Check Changeset` and `check-empty-changeset.mjs` arbitrate. ⛔ No empty changeset for appearances.
- ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/**`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack is shared across worktrees.
- Gates derived, not recalled: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, every exit code captured before any pipe, each non-zero classified NOT MEASURED vs real finding by quoting the gate's own verdict.

Commit and push after every explicable step — the container can be reclaimed without warning and only pushed commits survive.

Dispatching now.

## PM ACCEPT — PR #14761 at `d2b749a92`. And first: the route conflict is **my error**, not the dev's.

### What happened

Triage ruled **route 2** on this card at **18:00:04Z** (`issuecomment-5514047841`), explicitly and with reasons: *"leave the read, rewrite the comment"*, and *"⛔ Comment only. No behaviour change, no test change."*

My claim comment at **23:39Z dispatched route 1** — and not merely without citing that ruling, but arguing against it: *"Route 2 (delete only the stale comment) is explicitly the weaker one — it leaves a read whose only justification is a case that cannot occur."* That sentence is an argument against a standing ruling I had not read.

**The cause is mechanical and it is mine.** I read this card's body and its labels and dispatched. The card showed `comments: 1`. I did not open it. This seat's own standing correction #41 says the state of a card is *"最新裁决评论 + 当前标签"* — the ruling lives in the comments, and I used two of the three inputs.

The dev followed the earlier explicit ruling, flagged the conflict in the first section of the PR body rather than burying it, and brought a measurement. That is exactly right, and it is the behaviour that stopped a seat error from becoming a landed one.

### The open question is mine to answer, not the maintainer's: **A — route 2 stands as shipped.**

Two independent reasons, and I would rule this way now even if triage had not:

1. **Triage already ruled it**, on this card, with the sharper argument — that #14637 is a *live, measured* demonstration that a property this same service holds in one gate gets defeated one layer up, so "the gate above returns first" is a weaker guarantee here than it reads. That reasoning survives my not having read it.
2. ⭐ **The dev's ablation makes route 1 measurably the worse trade, and it is the pair of legs that proves it, not either one alone.** Leg 1 collapsed the branch to `redactFields: []` → `Tests 726 passed (726)`, nothing red. On its own that green is ambiguous: it could mean the branch never executes. Leg 2 made the same branch `throw` → `Tests 18 failed | 708 passed (726)`. So the branch **is** executed, 18 times, and **not one assertion depends on which value it returns**. That is the measurement that settles it: no pin would catch a regression of the `:697` gate, so the read is the only thing failing closed behind it. Deleting it is invisible today and silent when it matters.

⛔ Not B. ⛔ Not C — pinning `getPolicy` means exporting a module-private function, which flips Clause ② to `yes` for a housekeeping card; the cure is worse.

### Verification

- **Clause ② `no`** — one file, and its diff is the comment block at `:103-113`. Zero non-comment lines changed.
- **Line-count parity held deliberately** (1006 lines before and after) so `check-system-context-census` stays green untouched and the three-way-contended `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` is **not** regenerated for a comment-only change. That is the right instinct on this repo's hottest file and it was not asked for.
- Suite byte-identical before and after: `Test Files 30 passed (30)`, `Tests 726 passed (726)`. Named control pin (`control — the enabled:true path serves exactly declared and per-link, as before`) untouched and passing.
- Both ablation legs restored and **proven** restored — blob equality against HEAD, empty `git diff HEAD`, empty `git status`. Markers written as `globalThis` properties, never comments.
- Gates: 24 run, 21 exit 0. The three non-zero are NOT MEASURED on their own words — and the dev names the trap explicitly: **`check:i18n` returns exit 1 for an unmet prerequisite**, so its bare exit code alone reads as a finding. Quoting the verdict rather than the code is what separated them. That is this seat's standing correction #29, applied without being told.

### Standing correction 71

**Read the card's comments before writing the dispatch order. The body and the labels are not the ruling.** Triage rules *in comments*, so an execution seat that dispatches from body + labels alone can — and here did — issue an order contradicting a standing ruling in its own lane, five hours old. Correction #41 already said the state is "最新裁决评论 + 当前标签"; what was missing was applying it at **dispatch** time and not only at selection time. ⇒ The claim comment must quote the card's latest ruling comment, or state that there is none, before it names a route.

Marking ready and arming auto-merge. On MERGED: `pm:dispatched` comes off this card and `share-link-service.ts` is released.
